narrative.overview:
Each tool is a room drenched in its section's color. One original glass object per tool sits in the room under a light the cursor carries: the specular bloom and rim light slide toward the pointer, the object tilts toward it, its pieces parallax by depth, and its floor shadow swings the other way. Beside the object, a large light-weight title, one plain subtitle, three bulleted promises and a single pill action. Scanning happens in the same room: the object glides into the center of a progress ring cut from the section's gradient, and comes back to rest at the head of the results.

The system is native macOS through and through: SF Pro only, SF Symbols as the only glyph source, the real sidebar vibrancy material, system materials under lists. What makes it its own is color and light, not chrome. Dark appearance is a deep two-hue field with a soft light pool behind the object; light appearance is the same hue made luminous, pale top to pale bottom with the same pool. Nothing ships as a raster: every object, tile and ground is drawn in code from a small set of glass primitives.

Density is low on the front door and normal on the working screens. A tool's intro is a single viewport with lots of air; once the tool has been used it reopens compact, button first, so returning users reach the task faster.
keyCharacteristics: Seven color worlds (six sections plus Settings graphite), each nine colors; a world drenches ground, sidebar tint, list panels, tiles, ring and control tint together.
One glass hero object per tool on a 300pt stage, lit by a pointer-driven light; static at rest under Reduce Motion.
Light-weight display titles (40 / 32 / 28pt) with negative tracking; semibold only for labels and the action.
One capsule primary action per screen, inverted between appearances.
Rounded gradient tiles with white SF Symbols as the bullet and sidebar icon.

rules.name: The One Room Rule
rules.body: A screen belongs to exactly one world. Ground, sidebar tint, list panel tint, ring, pill and control tint all come from the selected tool's section; the only other worlds on screen are the sidebar's own row tiles, each carrying its section.

rules.name: The Derived Glass Rule
rules.body: Glass is never given its own colors. It is cut from four tints derived from the world: section glass (tile gradient, deep edge), spark glass (spark lifted 35% toward white), clear glass (white with a breath of glow), and pearl (white into spark mixed 62% toward white, mid edge).

rules.name: The Light Voice Rule
rules.body: Every title on a tool screen is light weight (300). Bold display type is not part of this system.

rules.name: The Object Is The Subject Rule
rules.body: At every width the hero object takes whatever space the text column leaves; the text column is capped, the object is not shrunk to make room for decoration.

rules.name: The Cursor Is The Light Rule
rules.body: Every highlight, rim, bevel, extrusion and floor shadow answers one shared light. At rest it sits top-left; the pointer pulls it across the object. Never paint a fixed highlight that disagrees with it.

rules.name: The Colored Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tinted with the world's deep or mid, never neutral black, except the hairline bevel of an engraved symbol (black 0.28).

dos: **Do** take every color on a tool screen from its section's world, including the control tint (tile bottom).
**Do** build any new hero object from the glass primitives and shape kit, at 300 x 300pt, with pieces assigned depths, and hide it from VoiceOver.
**Do** keep titles light weight (40 / 32 / 28pt) and reserve semibold for labels and the action.
**Do** put exactly one capsule primary action on a tool screen: white with a section label in dark rooms, section gradient with a white label in light rooms.
**Do** keep disabled actions readable (label at 0.62 white or 0.55 ink) on a quiet translucent pill.
**Do** stop all pointer tracking under Reduce Motion and fall back to crossfades.
**Do** write intro copy as a label plus one plain, true line per bullet, three bullets per tool.
donts: **Don't** paint a fixed highlight, gloss or shadow on glass that ignores the shared light, and don't tilt an object more than 8°.
**Don't** mix two worlds' grounds on one screen, or tint shadows neutral black.
**Don't** set tool titles in bold display type; the older bold welcome cards (30 and 34pt bold) are not part of this system.
**Don't** ship raster artwork, and never reuse MacPaw's artwork, icons, illustrations or branding; every object is original and drawn in code.
**Don't** wrap the room in an inset card or grey pane; the detail pane is the ground, full-bleed.
**Don't** let animation hold up a scan, review or clean.
